paite: Huan, huai thil khitin hichi ahia, Aigupta kumpipa uain pepa leh a tanghou bawlpan a pu uh Aigupta kumpipa a lungkimlousak ua.
english: It happened after these things, that the butler of the king of Egypt and his baker offended their lord, the king of Egypt.

paite: Huchiin, Pharo bel a sikha heutu nih tungah, a uain pia heutupen tungah leh a tanghou bawl heutupen tungah a hehta a.
english: Pharaoh was angry with his two officers, the chief cupbearer and the chief baker.

paite: Huchiin vengmi pawl heutu in ah, suangkulh, Joseph hena a omna ah, a tangsakta hi.
english: He put them in custody in the house of the captain of the guard, into the prison, the place where Joseph was bound.

paite: Huan, vengmi pawl heutu in Joseph bel amau a kemsaka, huchiin amau a na a sepsak ua, huan, ni bangzah hiam tak a tang uhi.
english: The captain of the guard assigned them to Joseph, and he took care of them. They stayed in prison many days.

paite: Huan, suangkulh a hena om, Aigupta kumpipa uain pepa leh tanghou bawlpa in, jan khat mang khiakna tuamtuam tuak a nei ua.
english: They both dreamed a dream, each man his dream, in one night, each man according to the interpretation of his dream, the cupbearer and the baker of the king of Egypt, who were bound in the prison.

paite: Huan, a jingin Joseph a kiang uah a valut a, amau a hong mu a, huan, ngaiin, a na lungkham mahmah uhi.
english: Joseph came in to them in the morning, and saw them, and saw that they were sad.

paite: Huchiin, aman, bang achia ahia tuniin lungkham mel po natel uchia? Chiin, Pharo sikha heutu, a pu inn a tang teita, a donga.
english: He asked Pharaoh’s officers who were with him in custody in his master’s house, saying, “Why do you look so sad today?”

paite: Huan, amau, a kiangah, mang ka nei ua, hon hilh chiansak thei kuamah lah a om ngal keia ahi, a chi ua. Huan, Joseph in, a kianguah, mang hilhchetna te Pathian a ahi ka hia? Hehpihtakin honhilh dih ua, achia.
english: They said to him, “We have dreamed a dream, and there is no one who can interpret it.” Joseph said to them, “Don’t interpretations belong to God? Please tell it to me.”

paite: Huchiin, uain pia heutu penin a mang Joseph a hilha, a kiangah, ngai dih, ka mangin, ka maah grepgui a hong om a;
english: The chief cupbearer told his dream to Joseph, and said to him, “In my dream, behold, a vine was in front of me,

paite: Grepgui ah ka thum a oma: huan, selnou bangin a hong om a, a pakte a hong om khia a; a pak bomten grep minte a hon omsak ua:
english: and in the vine were three branches. It was as though it budded, it blossomed, and its clusters produced ripe grapes.

paite: Huan, Pharo nou ka khut ah a hong om a; huchiin, grep, gahte ka loua, Pharo nou ah ka suak a, huai nou Pharo khut ah ka na pia a, achia.
english: Pharaoh’s cup was in my hand; and I took the grapes, and pressed them into Pharaoh’s cup, and I gave the cup into Pharaoh’s hand.”

paite: Huan, Joseph in, a kiangah, a hilhchetna hiai ahi: ka thumte ni thum ahia:
english: Joseph said to him, “This is its interpretation: the three branches are three days.

paite: Tua kipan ni thumin Pharo in na lutang a domkang dinga, na nasep mah a honsemsak nawn ding: huchiin a uain pepa na nahin laia na piak ngeina bangin, Pharo nou a khut ah na pe nawn ding hi.
english: Within three more days, Pharaoh will lift up your head, and restore you to your office. You will give Pharaoh’s cup into his hand, the way you did when you were his cupbearer.

paite: Ahihhangin na hong hamphat nawn chiangin hon theigige inla, hehpihtakin hehpihna ka tungah hon kilangsak inla, Pharo kiangah ka tungtang hon gen inla, hiai in a kipan honpi khia in:
english: But remember me when it will be well with you, and please show kindness to me, and make mention of me to Pharaoh, and bring me out of this house.

paite: Hebru te gam a kipan min a guka a honguk mang uh ka hia: hiai gamah leng khuk sunga a honkhum na ding in bangmah ka hihkhial kei hi, achia.
english: For indeed, I was stolen away out of the land of the Hebrews, and here also have I done nothing that they should put me into the dungeon.”

paite: Tanghou bawlpain hilhchetna a hoih chih a theih in, Joseph kiangah, ken leng mang ka neia, ngaiin, tanghou ngou lohbeu thum ka luin kana pua a:
english: When the chief baker saw that the interpretation was good, he said to Joseph, “I also was in my dream, and behold, three baskets of white bread were on my head.

paite: Huan, lohbeu tungnung penah Pharo an, tanghou bawlpa bawl, chi chih ana om a; huan, huaite vasaten lohbeu ka lu a ka puaka kipan a nane souhsouh ua, achia.
english: In the uppermost basket there was all kinds of baked food for Pharaoh, and the birds ate them out of the basket on my head.”

paite: Huan, Joseph in a dawnga, hiai a hilhchetna ahi: Lohbeu thum ni thum ahi;
english: Joseph answered, “This is its interpretation. The three baskets are three days.

paite: Tua kipan ni thum in Pharo in na pumpi akipanin na lutang a domkang dinga, sing dawn ah a hon khai ding; huchiin, vasaten na sa a ne souhsouh ding uh, achia.
english: Within three more days, Pharaoh will lift up your head from off you, and will hang you on a tree; and the birds will eat your flesh from off you.”

paite: Huan, hichi ahia, a ni thum ni, Pharo pian tanphak niin, aman a sikha tengteng a dingin ankuang a luia: huan, a sikhate laka uain pia heutupen lutang a domkang ta a.
english: It happened the third day, which was Pharaoh’s birthday, that he made a feast for all his servants, and he lifted up the head of the chief cupbearer and the head of the chief baker among his servants.

paite: Huan, uain pia heutu pen uain pemi mah in apangsak nawna; huchiin, nou Pharo khut ah a peta a:
english: He restored the chief cupbearer to his position again, and he gave the cup into Pharaoh’s hand;

paite: Ahihhangin, Joseph in amau a hilhchet bangtakin, tanghou bawl heutupen bel a khaita hi.Himahleh, uain pia heutu penin Joseph a theigige zenzen kei a, a mangnghilh maimah.
english: but he hanged the chief baker, as Joseph had interpreted to them.

paite: Himahleh, uain pia heutu penin Joseph a theigige zenzen kei a, a mangnghilh maimah.
english: Yet the chief cupbearer didn’t remember Joseph, but forgot him.
